title: Real conversation
goal: Tell a friend what happened, react to their news, keep a chat going with fillers and particles, and say 'the one who…' and 'he said that…'.
intro:
Real Odia conversation runs on small words. Friends react with **ଆରେ!**, **ସତରେ?**, **ବାପରେ!** and **କ'ଣ କହୁଛ!**; they buy time with **ମାନେ…** 'I mean…' and **କଥା କ'ଣ କି…** 'the thing is…'; and they colour every sentence with the particles **ତ** and **ହିଁ** and the everyday intensifiers **ପୂରା** 'totally' and **ଜମା** '(not) at all'.

This unit gives you all of that, plus the two structures you need to retell anything: **relative clauses** ('the girl *who* came yesterday', 'the place *where* we have tea') and **reported speech** ('he said *that*…'), including the very Odia quotative **ବୋଲି**. It closes Part 1: from here on, the course is about real life with friends and around town.

vocab.note: The most common filler in Odia speech. Also a noun: ଏହାର ମାନେ କ'ଣ? 'what does this mean?'
Goes after the word it colours: ମୁଁ ତ କହିଥିଲି 'I *did* tell you'. At the end of a question it asks for agreement: ସବୁ ଭଲ ତ? 'all good, right?'
ଏବେ ହିଁ 'right now', ସେ ହିଁ 'he himself / he of all people'. Colloquially often shortened to -ହିଁ joined to the word or replaced by ଇ: ସେଇ, ଏଇ.
The everyday word for "but"; କିନ୍ତୁ is a little more careful.
Only with friends and people younger than you; with elders say ଆଜ୍ଞା or just their name.
For good or bad surprise. Also ମା'ଲୋ (malo) "oh mother!", heard more from women.
ଆଉ କ'ଣ ଖବର? 'what's new?'; ଖବର କାଗଜ 'newspaper'.
କଥା ହେବା 'to talk, have a chat'; ସେ କଥା ଛାଡ଼ 'forget that'.
ଗପ କରିବା 'to chat'. Colloquially also ଗପିବା 'to chat, to talk a lot'.
Impersonal: ରିନା ସହ ମୋର ଦେଖା ହେଲା 'I ran into Rina' (lit. 'my seeing with Rina happened'). For a planned meeting use ଭେଟିବା.
Then ତା'ପରେ "after that" and ଶେଷରେ "in the end": the three words that hold any story together.
ମୁଁ ତାଙ୍କୁ ଚିହ୍ନେ 'I know him'. Knowing a fact is ଜାଣିବା.
ଝଗଡ଼ା କରିବା "to argue, fight"; ଝଗଡ଼ା ହେବା "a fight happens".
Answered by ସେ in the main clause. Respectful: ଯେଉଁମାନେ / ଯିଏ … ସେ (with -ନ୍ତି verb).

vocab.en: which, the … that (relative, before a noun)
vocab.note: Answered by ସେହି / ସେ.
Answered by ସେଠି "there".
Answered by ସେତେବେଳେ "then". Not a question word: "when?" is କେବେ / କେତେବେଳେ.
Answered by ତାହା / ସେଇଟା "that".

vocab.en: (quotative) closes reported words or thoughts; so, because; called
vocab.note: ସେ ଆସିବ ବୋଲି କହିଲା 'he said he'd come'; ଅସୁସ୍ଥ ବୋଲି ଆସିଲା ନାହିଁ 'didn't come because he's ill'; ମୋତେ ପାଗଳ ବୋଲି କହିଲା 'called me crazy'.
Colloquial intensifier: ପୂରା ପାଗଳ 'totally crazy', ପୂରା ସତ 'absolutely true'.
Always with ନାହିଁ / ନୁହେଁ: ଜମା ଭଲ ଲାଗିଲା ନାହିଁ 'I didn't like it at all'. The careful equivalent is ଆଦୌ.
Between friends it is affectionate teasing; about a stranger it is rude.
English loan used everywhere: ଟେନସନ୍ ନେବା 'to stress out', ଟେନସନ୍ ନିଅ ନାହିଁ 'don't worry'. The native word is ଚିନ୍ତା.
ବାସ୍, ଆଉ ନୁହେଁ 'that's it, no more'. In a story: …ବାସ୍! 'and that was that!'

phrases.en: Hey, you're here! / Fancy seeing you here! (familiar)

phrases.note: The standard opener with friends. Answer: ସବୁ ଠିକ୍ "all fine" or ଏଇ ଚାଲିଛି "just carrying on".

phrases.en: Listen, I'll tell you something funny.
I mean… what I was saying was…
I did tell you! / I told you so!

phrases.note: To a ତୁ-friend: ଟେନସନ୍ ନେ ନାହିଁ. Polite: ଚିନ୍ତା କରନ୍ତୁ ନାହିଁ.

grammar.title: Relative clauses: ଯେ- … ସେ- pairs and -ଥିବା
grammar.body:
English puts 'who / which / where' *after* the noun ('the girl who came'). Odia does it the other way round: the relative clause comes **first**, opened by a **ଯ-word**, and the main clause answers it with a matching **ସ/ତ-word**:

ଯିଏ … ସେ — (the one) who … he/she
ଯେଉଁ + noun … ସେ / ସେହି — the (noun) which … that
ଯେଉଁଠି … ସେଠି — where … there
ଯେତେବେଳେ … ସେତେବେଳେ — when … then
ଯାହା … ତାହା — what … that

So 'the girl who came yesterday is my sister's friend' is literally 'which girl came yesterday, she is my sister's friend': ଯେଉଁ ଝିଅ କାଲି ଆସିଥିଲା, ସେ ମୋ ଅପାର ସାଙ୍ଗ. In relaxed speech the answering word is often dropped when it's obvious.

**The shortcut people use most**: a participle in front of the noun, like English 'the *sitting* boy'. **-ଥିବା** = 'who did / who has done', **-ଉଥିବା** = 'who is/was doing': କାଲି ଆସିଥିବା ଝିଅଟି 'the girl who came yesterday', ଫୋନ କରୁଥିବା ଲୋକ 'the person (who is) calling'. These never change for person or politeness.

**Trap**: ଯେତେବେଳେ is not a question. 'When are you coming?' is କେବେ ଆସିବ?, never ଯେତେବେଳେ.

grammar.title: Reported speech: ଯେ and ବୋଲି
grammar.body:
There are two ways to report what someone said or thought:

1. **verb + ଯେ + what was said** — like English 'said that…': ସେ କହିଲା **ଯେ** ସେ ଡେରିରେ ଆସିବ.
2. **what was said + ବୋଲି + verb** — the more typically Odia, more spoken way: ସେ ଡେରିରେ ଆସିବ **ବୋଲି** କହିଲା. Think of ବୋଲି as a spoken closing quotation mark.

**No change of tense**: Odia keeps the tense that was actually used. 'He said he *would* come' is literally 'he said he *will* come' (ଆସିବ). The same goes for questions: ସେ ପଚାରିଲା ତୁମେ କେଉଁଠି ଅଛ 'he asked where you are'.

**ବୋଲି with thinking**: ତୁମେ ରାଗିଛ ବୋଲି ମୁଁ ଭାବିଲି 'I thought you were angry'.

**ବୋଲି as 'because'**: a reason followed by ବୋଲି ('saying/being that…'): ସେ ଅସୁସ୍ଥ ବୋଲି ଆସିଲା ନାହିଁ 'he didn't come because he's ill'.

**ବୋଲି for names and labels**: ସେ ମୋତେ ପାଗଳ ବୋଲି କହିଲା 'he called me crazy'.

Direct quotes are very common in storytelling, often with the voice changed for effect: ବୋଉ କହିଲେ, “ଶୀଘ୍ର ଘରକୁ ଆସ।”

examples.native: ସେ କହିଲା ଯେ ସେ ଡେରିରେ ଆସିବ।
examples.roman: se kôhila je se ḍerire asibô.

examples.en: He said he'd be late. (more colloquial)
He didn't come because he's not well.

examples.native: ମୁଁ ଭାବିଲି ତୁମେ ଆଉ ଆସିବ ନାହିଁ।
examples.roman: muṃ bhabili tume au asibô nahiṃ.
examples.en: I thought you weren't coming any more.

grammar.title: Sounding natural: particles, fillers and reactions
grammar.body:
**Particles** go straight after the word they colour:
**ତ** — 'after all / well / you know', with a touch of emphasis or mild protest: ମୁଁ ତ ଜାଣେ ନାହିଁ 'well, *I* don't know'; ମୁଁ ତ କହିଥିଲି 'I *did* tell you'. At the end of a question it asks for agreement: ସବୁ ଭଲ ତ? 'everything OK, right?'
**ହିଁ** — 'exactly / only / the very': ଏବେ ହିଁ 'right now', ସେ ହିଁ 'he himself, *he* of all people'. In fast speech it fuses: ସେଇ, ଏଇ.
**ବି** — 'also, even'; **ନା** at the end — '…, right?'; **କି** at the end — turns a statement into a yes/no question.

**Fillers** to hold the floor: ମାନେ… 'I mean…', କଥା କ'ଣ କି… 'the thing is…', ଦେଖ… 'look…', ହଉ 'okay', ଆଚ୍ଛା 'right…'.

**Reactions** keep the other person talking: ସତରେ? 'really?', ବାପରେ! 'wow / oh no!', ଆରେ! 'hey! oh!', କ'ଣ କହୁଛ! 'no way!', ତା'ପରେ? 'and then?', ହଁ ହଁ 'yeah, yeah'.

**Intensifiers**: ପୂରା 'totally' (ପୂରା ପାଗଳ), and ଜମା '(not) at all', which only goes with a negative: ଜମା ଭଲ ଲାଗିଲା ନାହିଁ.

**Trap**: ଆରେ, ତୁ and ପାଗଳ are for friends. With elders, use ଆଜ୍ଞା, ଆପଣ and a calmer ସତରେ?

examples.en: Well, I don't know (don't ask me).
Come on, let's go right now.

examples.native: ମାନେ, ଖାଇବା ଭଲ ଥିଲା, ହେଲେ ପୂରା ଥଣ୍ଡା।
examples.roman: mane, khaiba bhôlô thila, hele pura thôṇḍa.
examples.en: I mean, the food was good, but stone cold.

culture:
Chatting (ଗପ କରିବା) is a serious pastime in Odisha: over tea at the neighbourhood *chhak* (junction), on the veranda in the evening, at the college canteen, or in a family WhatsApp group that never sleeps. A good listener reacts all the time: ହଁ ହଁ, ସତରେ?, ବାପରେ!, ତା'ପରେ? Silence sounds like boredom.

With close friends of your age, young Odias quickly drop to **ତୁ** and tease each other freely (ପାଗଳ, ବାହାନା!); with someone you've just met, or anyone older, stay with **ତୁମେ** or **ଆପଣ**, and leave out ଆରେ. Everyday talk mixes in English freely: *tension*, *sorry*, *plan*, *seriously*. Odia spoken in Cuttack and Bhubaneswar is the standard you hear on TV; in western Odisha you'll hear Sambalpuri (Kosli), and in the south Berhampur Odia, both with their own words and tunes, so don't be surprised if a friend from Sambalpur sounds different. Puri's flaky sweet **khaja** (ଖଜା), bought outside the Jagannath temple, is the classic thing to bring back from a trip.

tip.title: Reacting, and the particles ତ and ହିଁ
tip.body:
- React all the time: **ସତରେ?** 'really?', **ବାପରେ!** 'wow!', **କ'ଣ କହୁଛ!** 'no way!', **ଆରେ!** 'hey!' (friends only).
- **ତ** after a word adds 'after all / well': ମୁଁ **ତ** ଜାଣେ ନାହିଁ. At the end: ସବୁ ଭଲ **ତ**? 'all good, right?'
- **ହିଁ** means 'exactly / the very': ଏବେ **ହିଁ** 'right now', ସେ **ହିଁ** '*he* of all people'.

sentences.en: Wow, what a crowd!

sentences.native: କ'ଣ କହୁଛ! ଭାଇନା ବାହାହେବେ?
sentences.roman: kôṇô kôhuchhô! bhaina bahahebe?
sentences.en: No way! Your big brother's getting married?

sentences.native: ଆରେ, ତୁମେ ଏଠି କ'ଣ କରୁଛ?
sentences.roman: are, tume eṭhi kôṇô kôruchhô?

sentences.en: Come on, let's call right now.

tip.title: First, then, in the end
tip.body:
- Tie a story together with **ପ୍ରଥମେ** 'first', **ତା'ପରେ** 'then', **ହଠାତ୍** 'suddenly', **ଶେଷରେ** 'in the end'.
- Running into someone is impersonal: (ମୋର) ରିନା **ସହ ଦେଖା ହେଲା** 'I ran into Rina'.
- Use **-ଇଥିଲି** for things that happened a while ago, **-ଇଲି** for just now.

sentences.native: କାଲି ବଜାରରେ ମୋ ପୁରୁଣା ସାଙ୍ଗ ସହ ଦେଖା ହେଲା।
sentences.roman: kali bôjarôre mo puruṇa saṅgô sôhô dekha hela.
sentences.en: Yesterday I ran into an old friend at the market.

sentences.native: ପ୍ରଥମେ ମୁଁ ତାକୁ ଚିହ୍ନିପାରିଲି ନାହିଁ।
sentences.roman: prôthôme muṃ taku chinhiparili nahiṃ.
sentences.en: At first I couldn't recognise him.

sentences.native: ତା'ପରେ ଆମେ ଘଣ୍ଟେ ଗପ କଲୁ।
sentences.roman: tapôre ame ghôṇṭe gôpô kôlu.
sentences.en: Then we chatted for an hour.

sentences.native: ଶୁଣ, ଆଜି ଅଫିସରେ ଗୋଟିଏ ମଜା କଥା ହେଲା।
sentences.roman: suṇô, aji ôphisôre goṭie môja kôtha hela.
sentences.en: Listen, something funny happened at the office today.

sentences.native: ତା'ପରେ? ସେମାନେ ଝଗଡ଼ା କଲେ?
sentences.roman: tapôre? semane jhôgôṛa kôle?
sentences.en: And then? Did they have a fight?

sentences.native: ନା, ଝଗଡ଼ା ହେଲା ନାହିଁ, ଶେଷରେ ସମସ୍ତେ ହସିଲେ।
sentences.roman: na, jhôgôṛa hela nahiṃ, sesôre sômôste hôsile.
sentences.en: No, there was no fight; in the end everyone laughed.

sentences.native: ଏ କଥା ବୋଉକୁ କୁହ ନାହିଁ।
sentences.roman: e kôtha bouku kuhô nahiṃ.
sentences.en: Don't tell Mum about this.

sentences.native: ତୁମେ ମୋତେ ଚିହ୍ନିଲ?
sentences.roman: tume mote chinhilô?
sentences.en: Do you recognise me?

sentences.native: ଆଜି ସଞ୍ଜରେ ଚା ଦୋକାନରେ ଗପ କରିବା।
sentences.roman: aji sôñjôre cha dokanôre gôpô kôriba.
sentences.en: Let's chat at the tea stall this evening.

lessons.title: The one who…, the place where…

tip.title: ଯ-word first, ସ-word answers
tip.body:
- The 'who/where/when' clause comes **first**, then a matching word answers it: **ଯିଏ … ସେ**, **ଯେଉଁ … ସେ**, **ଯେଉଁଠି … ସେଠି**, **ଯେତେବେଳେ … ସେତେବେଳେ**, **ଯାହା … ତାହା**.
- Shortcut: **-ଥିବା** before a noun = 'who did': କାଲି ଆସିଥିବା ଝିଅଟି.
- ଯେତେବେଳେ is never a question ('when?' = କେବେ).

sentences.native: ଯିଏ ପ୍ରଥମେ ପହଞ୍ଚିବ, ସେ ଜାଗା ରଖିବ।
sentences.roman: jie prôthôme pôhôñchibô, se jaga rôkhibô.
sentences.en: Whoever gets there first keeps a place.

sentences.native: ଯେଉଁ ପିଲା ଫୋନ କରିଥିଲା, ସେ ମୋ ଭାଇର ସାଙ୍ଗ।
sentences.roman: jeuṃ pila phonô kôrithila, se mo bhairô saṅgô.
sentences.en: The kid who called is my brother's friend.

sentences.native: ମୁଁ ଯେଉଁଠି କାମ କରେ, ସେଠି ଭଲ ଚା ମିଳେ ନାହିଁ।
sentences.roman: muṃ jeuṃṭhi kamô kôre, seṭhi bhôlô cha miḷe nahiṃ.
sentences.en: You can't get good tea where I work.

sentences.native: ଯେତେବେଳେ ମୁଁ ଫୋନ କଲି, ସେତେବେଳେ ସେ ଶୋଇଥିଲା।
sentences.roman: jetebeḷe muṃ phonô kôli, setebeḷe se soithila.
sentences.en: When I called, he was asleep.

sentences.native: ତୁମେ ଯାହା କହିଲ, ମୁଁ ତାହା ବୁଝିଲି।
sentences.roman: tume jaha kôhilô, muṃ taha bujhili.
sentences.en: I understood what you said.

sentences.native: କାଲି ଆସିଥିବା ଝିଅଟି କିଏ?
sentences.roman: kali asithiba jhiôṭi kie?
sentences.en: Who was the girl who came yesterday?

sentences.native: ସେଠି ବସିଥିବା ପିଲାଟି ମୋ ଭାଇ।
sentences.roman: seṭhi bôsithiba pilaṭi mo bhai.
sentences.en: The kid sitting over there is my brother.

sentences.native: ଯିଏ ଡେରିରେ ଆସିବ, ସେ ଚା ପଇସା ଦେବ।
sentences.roman: jie ḍerire asibô, se cha pôisa debô.
sentences.en: Whoever comes late pays for the tea.

sentences.native: ଯେଉଁ ସାଙ୍ଗ ସହ କାଲି ଦେଖା ହେଲା, ତାର ନାମ ମନେପଡ଼ୁନି।
sentences.roman: jeuṃ saṅgô sôhô kali dekha hela, tarô namô mônepôṛuni.
sentences.en: I can't remember the name of the friend I ran into yesterday.

tip.title: Reporting with ଯେ and ବୋଲି
tip.body:
- **said + ଯେ + words**: ସେ କହିଲା **ଯେ** ସେ ଆସିବ.
- More spoken: **words + ବୋଲି + said**: ସେ ଆସିବ **ବୋଲି** କହିଲା.
- Keep the original tense: 'he said he'd come' = ଆସିବ ('will come').
- ବୋଲି also gives a reason ('…so'): ଅସୁସ୍ଥ **ବୋଲି** ଆସିଲା ନାହିଁ.

sentences.native: ସେ କ'ଣ କହିଲା? ଆସିବ ନା ନାହିଁ?
sentences.roman: se kôṇô kôhila? asibô na nahiṃ?
sentences.en: What did he say? Is he coming or not?

sentences.native: ସେ ଆସିବ ବୋଲି କହିଲା, କିନ୍ତୁ ଆସିଲା ନାହିଁ।
sentences.roman: se asibô boli kôhila, kintu asila nahiṃ.
sentences.en: He said he'd come, but he didn't.

sentences.native: ଅପା କହିଲେ ଯେ ତାଙ୍କର ଚାକିରି ମିଳିଗଲା।
sentences.roman: ôpa kôhile je taṅkôrô chakiri miḷigôla.
sentences.en: My sister said she got the job.

sentences.native: ତୁମେ ରାଗିଛ ବୋଲି ମୁଁ ଭାବିଲି।
sentences.roman: tume ragichhô boli muṃ bhabili.
sentences.en: I thought you were angry.

sentences.native: ମୁଁ ତ କହିଥିଲି, ସେ ଡେରିରେ ଆସିବ!
sentences.roman: muṃ tô kôhithili, se ḍerire asibô!
sentences.en: I told you he'd be late!

sentences.native: ସେ ପଚାରିଲା ତୁମେ କେଉଁଠି ଅଛ।
sentences.roman: se pôcharila tume keuṃṭhi ôchhô.
sentences.en: He asked where you are.

sentences.native: ତୁ ପାଗଳ କି? ଏତେ ରାତିରେ କିଏ ଫୋନ କରେ?
sentences.roman: tu pagôḷô ki? ete ratire kie phonô kôre?
sentences.en: Are you crazy? Who calls this late at night?

sentences.native: ଭାଇ ଅସୁସ୍ଥ ବୋଲି ଆଜି କଲେଜ ଗଲା ନାହିଁ।
sentences.roman: bhai ôsusthô boli aji kôlejô gôla nahiṃ.
sentences.en: My brother didn't go to college today because he's not well.

sentences.native: ବୋଉ କହିଲେ, “ରାତି ଦଶଟା ଆଗରୁ ଘରେ ପହଞ୍ଚିବୁ।”
sentences.roman: bou kôhile, “rati dôsôṭa agôru ghôre pôhôñchibu.”
sentences.en: Mum said, 'Be home before ten.'

sentences.native: ସେ ମୋତେ ପାଗଳ ବୋଲି କହିଲା!
sentences.roman: se mote pagôḷô boli kôhila!
sentences.en: He called me crazy!

tip.title: Fillers and "but"
tip.body:
- **ମାନେ…** 'I mean…' and **କଥା କ'ଣ କି…** 'the thing is…' buy you time and soften what comes next.
- **ହେଲେ** is the everyday 'but'; **ଯଦିଓ** 'although' opens the first half.
- **ଏମିତି** 'like this' / **ସେମିତି** 'like that'.

sentences.native: ମାନେ, ମୁଁ ଆସିବି, ହେଲେ ଟିକେ ଡେରି ହେବ।
sentences.roman: mane, muṃ asibi, hele ṭike ḍeri hebô.
sentences.en: I mean, I'll come, but I'll be a bit late.

sentences.native: କଥା କ'ଣ କି, ମୋ ପାଖରେ ଏବେ ପଇସା ନାହିଁ।
sentences.roman: kôtha kôṇô ki, mo pakhôre ebe pôisa nahiṃ.
sentences.en: The thing is, I don't have any money right now.

sentences.native: ଏମିତି କୁହ ନାହିଁ।
sentences.roman: emiti kuhô nahiṃ.
sentences.en: Don't say that. (lit. don't speak like this)

sentences.native: ସେ ସବୁବେଳେ ସେମିତି କରେ।
sentences.roman: se sôbubeḷe semiti kôre.
sentences.en: He always does that.

sentences.native: ଯଦିଓ ବର୍ଷା ହେଉଥିଲା, ଆମେ ବାହାରକୁ ଗଲୁ।
sentences.roman: jôdio bôrsa heuthila, ame baharôku gôlu.
sentences.en: Although it was raining, we went out.

sentences.native: ଖାଇବା ଭଲ ଥିଲା, ହେଲେ ବହୁତ ରାଗ।
sentences.roman: khaiba bhôlô thila, hele bôhutô ragô.
sentences.en: The food was good, but really spicy.

sentences.native: ମାନେ… ମୁଁ କହୁଥିଲି କି, କାଲି ଆମେ ପୁରୀ ଯିବା?
sentences.roman: mane… muṃ kôhuthili ki, kali ame Puri jiba?
sentences.en: I mean… what I was saying was, shall we go to Puri tomorrow?

sentences.native: ଯଦିଓ ସେ ମୋ ସାଙ୍ଗ, ମୁଁ ତାକୁ ସବୁ କଥା କହେ ନାହିଁ।
sentences.roman: jôdio se mo saṅgô, muṃ taku sôbu kôtha kôhe nahiṃ.
sentences.en: Although he's my friend, I don't tell him everything.

sentences.native: ଏମିତି ହିଁ ହୁଏ।
sentences.roman: emiti hiṃ hue.
sentences.en: That's just how it goes.

tip.title: ପୂରା, ଜମା, ବାସ୍
tip.body:
- **ପୂରା** 'totally': ପୂରା ପାଗଳ, ପୂରା ସତ.
- **ଜମା** '(not) at all' needs a negative: **ଜମା** ଭଲ ଲାଗିଲା **ନାହିଁ**.
- **ବାସ୍** 'that's it, enough'. To calm a friend: **ଟେନସନ୍ ନିଅ ନାହିଁ**.

sentences.native: ଟେନସନ୍ ନିଅ ନାହିଁ, ସବୁ ଠିକ୍ ହୋଇଯିବ।
sentences.roman: ṭensôn niô nahiṃ, sôbu ṭhik hoijibô.
sentences.en: Don't stress, it'll all work out.

sentences.native: ମୋତେ ଜମା ଭଲ ଲାଗିଲା ନାହିଁ।
sentences.roman: mote jôma bhôlô lagila nahiṃ.
sentences.en: I didn't like it at all.

sentences.native: ସେ ପୂରା ପାଗଳ।
sentences.roman: se pura pagôḷô.
sentences.en: He's totally crazy.

sentences.native: ଏ କଥା ପୂରା ଅଦ୍ଭୁତ!
sentences.roman: e kôtha pura ôdbhutô!
sentences.en: That's really weird!

sentences.native: ଛାଡ଼ ସେ କଥା, ଚାଲ ଚା ପିଇବା।
sentences.roman: chhaṛô se kôtha, chalô cha piiba.
sentences.en: Forget it, let's have some tea.

sentences.native: ମୁଁ ତାକୁ ଜମା ଚିହ୍ନେ ନାହିଁ।
sentences.roman: muṃ taku jôma chinhe nahiṃ.
sentences.en: I don't know him at all.

sentences.native: ବାସ୍, ଆଉ ଝଗଡ଼ା ନୁହେଁ!
sentences.roman: bas, au jhôgôṛa nuheṃ!
sentences.en: That's it, no more fighting!

sentences.native: ହଉ, ବାସ୍! ମୁଁ ବୁଝିଗଲି।
sentences.roman: hôu, bas! muṃ bujhigôli.
sentences.en: Okay, enough! I get it.

sentences.native: ପରୀକ୍ଷା ପାଇଁ ଏତେ ଟେନସନ୍ କାହିଁକି?
sentences.roman: pôrikhya paiṃ ete ṭensôn kahiṃki?
sentences.en: Why so stressed about the exam?

sentences.native: ମୋ ଫୋନ ପୂରା ଖରାପ ହୋଇଗଲା।
sentences.roman: mo phonô pura khôrapô hoigôla.
sentences.en: My phone's completely dead.
